subject: series
synopsis: A classic 2000AD horror/war strip following Nazi soldiers on the Eastern Front who encounter a Romanian patrol with a terrifying secret, mixing WWII history with vampire mythology in a bleak and effective way.
author: Gerry Finley-Day

subject: series
synopsis: John Wagner and Carlos Ezquerra's fascist future lawman of Mega-City One, the flagship of 2000 AD since 1977: satire, action and long-form epics like The Apocalypse War, Necropolis and America.
author: John Wagner, Alan Grant

subject: series
synopsis: DC's flagship anthology that introduced Superman in 1938 and became his longest-running title, through the Golden, Silver and Bronze Ages.
author: Jerry Siegel, Otto Binder

subject: series
synopsis: Batman's home since Detective Comics #27 (1939) — Englehart and Rogers, O'Neil and Adams, and the Bronze Age detective stories — DC's namesake title.
author: Bill Finger, Gardner Fox

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's flagship mutant title, defined by Chris Claremont's sixteen-year run with Cockrum, Byrne and Smith — Dark Phoenix, Days of Future Past — through the Lobdell and Brubaker eras.
author: Chris Claremont, Scott Lobdell

subject: series
synopsis: Batman's own title from 1940 to 2011, from Finger and Kane's Golden Age through O'Neil and Adams, Moench, Knightfall and Hush.
author: Bill Finger, Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Parker's flagship title from Lee and Ditko's 1963 debut through Romita, Conway's death of Gwen Stacy, Stern, Michelinie and McFarlane, Straczynski and Slott.
author: Dan Slott, David Michelinie

subject: series
synopsis: The satirical humor magazine founded by Harvey Kurtzman and William Gaines at EC in 1952; the 'usual gang of idiots' — Jaffee's Fold-Ins, Spy vs. Spy, Don Martin — shaped American comedy for seven decades.

subject: series
synopsis: Jolly Blackburn's long-running slice-of-life comedy about tabletop RPG players. Consistently funny, surprisingly emotionally rich over its run, and the most accurate portrayal of gaming culture in any comic medium.
author: Jolly Blackburn

subject: series
synopsis: Todd McFarlane's creator-owned supernatural anti-hero defined Image Comics' early identity. Al Simmons as a hellspawn navigating cosmic good-vs-evil mythology. Spectacular art; plotting became increasingly dense. A milestone for creator rights.
author: Todd McFarlane

subject: series
synopsis: Superman's own title from 1939: the Golden and Silver Age adventures, Curt Swan's long Bronze Age, the post-Byrne Adventures of Superman years and the return to Superman #650-714.
author: Karl Kesel, Jerry Ordway

subject: series
synopsis: Archie Andrews, Betty, Veronica and the Riverdale gang in the flagship Archie title (1942-2015) — gag-a-page teen humor drawn by Harry Lucey, Dan DeCarlo and Stan Goldberg.
author: Frank Doyle, George Gladir

subject: series
synopsis: Anthology series best known for Barry Windsor-Smith's 'Weapon X' — one of the finest single stories in Marvel history. The surrounding material is mostly disposable but the format allowed experimental short-form work.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Captain America's own title from 1968: Lee, Kirby and Steranko, Englehart's Secret Empire, Stern and Byrne, Mark Gruenwald's ten-year run, and the later relaunches gathered on this shelf.
author: Mark Gruenwald, J. Michael Straczynski

subject: series
synopsis: Lee and Kirby's 1961 founding of the Marvel Age — Galactus, the Silver Surfer, Doctor Doom — and the later runs of Byrne, Simonson and DeFalco, through #416.
author: Stan Lee, Tom DeFalco

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Murdock's original series (1964-1998): Gene Colan's long run, Frank Miller's Elektra saga and Born Again, and Ann Nocenti's tenure.
author: Ann Nocenti, D. G. Chichester

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's flagship team book (1963-1996): Lee and Kirby's founding, Thomas's Kree-Skrull War, Englehart's Celestial Madonna and Stern's Under Siege.
author: Roy Thomas, Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: Journey into Mystery renumbered as Thor in 1966: Lee and Kirby's cosmic Asgard, then Walt Simonson's acclaimed run (#337-382), through DeFalco and Jurgens.
author: Tom DeFalco, Gerry Conway

subject: series
synopsis: The Hulk's long first series: Herb Trimpe's 1970s, Bill Mantlo's tenure and Peter David's twelve-year run (#331-467) that remade Bruce Banner.
author: Peter David, Bill Mantlo

subject: series
synopsis: Green Lantern volume 3 (1990-2004): Hal Jordan's return and fall into Parallax in Emerald Twilight, then Kyle Rayner as the last Green Lantern.
author: John Broome, Dennis O'Neil

subject: series
synopsis: Hal Jordan's Silver Age series by John Broome and Gil Kane, then O'Neil and Adams's socially conscious Green Lantern/Green Arrow and the Green Lantern Corps era.
author: John Broome, Dennis O'Neil

subject: series
synopsis: Tony Stark's first solo series (1968-1996): Michelinie and Layton's Demon in a Bottle and Armor Wars, and O'Neil's Obadiah Stane saga.
author: Gerry Conway, Robert Kanigher

subject: series
synopsis: Wolverine's first ongoing (1988-2003): Claremont and Buscema's Madripoor stories, then Larry Hama's long run with Silvestri and Kubert.
author: Larry Hama, Frank Tieri

subject: series
synopsis: DC's long-running horror anthology series that ran from 1951 to 1983, featuring supernatural tales hosted by Cain; a precursor to the Vertigo horror anthologies and later revived as a Vertigo title.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Dave Sim's landmark self-published series collected here, following the barbarian aardvark Cerebus through politics, religion, and philosophy in an epic independent comics milestone running 300 issues.
author: Dave Sim

subject: series
synopsis: The American edition of Metal Hurlant, publishing European and American adult science fiction and fantasy comics; an enormously influential showcase for Moebius, Enki Bilal, Richard Corben, and many others.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: The original X-Men reunited as X-Factor (1986), then Peter David's acclaimed government-team run with Havok, Strong Guy and Madrox (#71-89).
author: Louise Jones Simonson, Howard Mackie

subject: series
synopsis: Wonder Woman's original series (1942-1986): William Moulton Marston and H.G. Peter's Golden Age Amazon, then Robert Kanigher's long Silver Age tenure.
author: Robert Kanigher, William Marston

subject: series
synopsis: Warner Bros.' classic cartoon characters in comic form across Gold Key, DC, and other publishers. Bugs Bunny, Daffy, Tweety, and friends in consistently light-hearted all-ages humor. The best issues match the wit of the animated shorts.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: The horror movie magazine institution. Not comics in the traditional sense — interviews, reviews, production stills, and behind-the-scenes content on horror films. An essential document of horror culture for its era.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Nintendo's official magazine mixed gaming news with licensed comics adaptations of Mario, Zelda, Metroid, and others. The comics sections are charming artifacts; the magazine itself was a formative experience for a generation of gamers.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's long-running anthology (1938-1983): Superboy's home in the Silver Age and the birthplace of the Legion of Super-Heroes (#247).
author: Otto Binder, Robert Bernstein

subject: series
synopsis: Bronze Age issues of The Flash featuring Barry Allen's adventures during one of DC's most creatively fertile periods, including ties to the classic Crisis on Multiple Earths crossover events that established the multiverse concept.
author: Cary Bates

subject: series
synopsis: Wally West's Flash (1987-2009): Baron and Messner-Loebs, then Mark Waid's definitive run and Geoff Johns' rogues-focused tenure.
author: John Broome, Cary Bates

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Parker's second concurrent ongoing. 'Kraven's Last Hunt' (shared across all Spider-books) is the best story connected to this title. Bill Mantlo's long run is solid character-driven superhero work.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's original team book (1960-1987): Gardner Fox and Mike Sekowsky's Silver Age Justice League, the annual JSA crossovers, through Gerry Conway's Detroit era.
author: Gerry Conway, Gardner Fox

subject: series
synopsis: Canada's super-team in their own series (1983-1994): John Byrne's opening run, then Mantlo, Furman and Hudnall.
author: Bill Mantlo, Simon Furman

subject: series
synopsis: Bongo Comics' long-running tie-in series. Maintained surprising fidelity to the show's satirical voice. Consistently funny all-ages material with occasional standout issues that rival the show's best.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: George Pérez's 1987 mythological relaunch of Wonder Woman, then Messner-Loebs, Byrne, Jiménez and Greg Rucka's diplomatic run (#195-226).
author: Robert Kanigher, William Marston

subject: series
synopsis: The adjectiveless X-Men (1991-2001): Claremont and Jim Lee's record-breaking #1, then Lobdell and Kelly, into Morrison's New X-Men renumbering.
author: Joe Kelly, Chris Claremont
